name: Transformer / foundation models for well logs: WLFM (USTC 2025), LithoFormer (2026), TimeGPT for well logs (2024), TGS promptable ViT-MAE well-log foundation model (IMAGE 2025), CMT-enhanced Hiformer (Processes 2025)
authors_org: WLFM: Zhenyu Qi, Qing Yu, Jichen Wang, Yun-Bo Zhao, Zerui Li, Wenjun Lv (University of Science and Technology of China). LithoFormer: Shwetha Salimath, Francesca Bugiotti, Sylvain Wlodarczyk, Sohaib Ouzineb (CentraleSupelec / industry partner [uncertain]). TS foundation model: Ardiansyah Koeshidayatullah, Abdulrahman Al-Fakih, SanLinn Ismael Kaka (KFUPM [uncertain]). TGS: Ben Lasscock, Altay Sansal, Keyla Gonzalez, Alejandro Valenciano (TGS). CMT-Hiformer: authors of 'Stratigraphic Correlation of Well Logs Using Geology-Informed Deep Learning Networks' (Processes 13(5):1288, Shuanghe oil field team, China).
year: 2024 (TimeGPT well logs, Dec 2024), 2025 (WLFM Sep 2025; TGS IMAGE 2025; CMT-Hiformer Apr 2025), 2026 (LithoFormer Jul 2026)
venue_link: WLFM arXiv 2509.18152 https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18152 ; LithoFormer arXiv 2607.22804 https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22804 ; 'Leveraging Time-Series Foundation Model for Subsurface Well Logs Prediction and Anomaly Detection' arXiv 2412.05681 https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05681 ; TGS 'Well log foundation model - making promptable AI models for interpretation', SEG/AAPG IMAGE 2025 expanded abstract https://www.tgs.com/technical-library/well-log-foundation-model-making-promptable-ai-models-for-interpretation and https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/segeab/proceedings-abstract/SEGEAB.44/1/2910/725127 ; CMT-Hiformer, Processes 2025 https://doi.org/10.3390/pr13051288 ; related: Deep Hierarchical Graph Correlation (CNN + DP well-log alignment), JMSE 14(1):66 2026 https://doi.org/10.3390/jmse14010066
code_availability: None of the five releases public code or weights as far as found: WLFM paper gives no code/weight link; LithoFormer none (CC BY-NC-SA text only); TimeGPT is a closed commercial API (Nixtla); TGS model is proprietary (trained on 1.1M licensed logs); CMT-Hiformer no code found [uncertain]. Any use in Erudition means re-implementing the pretraining recipe on our own GR data.
evidence_level: WLFM, LithoFormer, TimeGPT-logs: arXiv preprints (abstract + HTML read for WLFM). CMT-Hiformer: peer-reviewed MDPI Processes (abstract/snippet only; full text 403). TGS: industry conference expanded abstract (summary page only). None evaluated on horizontal-well TVT/geosteering.
extreme_summary: Well-log transformers are now pretrained on 1k to 1.1M vertical wells with masked-patch reconstruction (WLFM VQ tokens + stratigraphy-aware cross-well contrastive loss; TGS ViT-MAE) and fine-tuned for lithology, porosity, formation tops or zonation, often with geology-informed losses (superposition/ordering penalties in LithoFormer and CMT-Hiformer). They give layer-aware GR embeddings and ordering constraints, but all target vertical-well interpretation, not lateral-to-typewell alignment.
task_definition: Vertical-well interpretation: per-depth lithology/zonation classification, porosity regression, formation-top depth prediction (TGS, prompted by formation name), missing-log imputation, anomaly detection, and cross-well stratigraphic correlation via layer-aware embeddings (WLFM) or boundary prediction (CMT-Hiformer, LithoFormer). Not geosteering: no model predicts TVT of a lateral against a typewell.
inputs: Multi-curve logs in depth: GR, SP, AC (sonic), resistivity, density, neutron (WLFM uses GR/SP/AC among others); TGS uses 1.1M North American logs of many curve types; TimeGPT uses single-curve series. No trajectory, no typewell pairing, no XY neighbours except WLFM's cross-well positive-pair mining by relative depth.
target_parameterisation: Per-depth class labels (lithology, zone), per-depth continuous properties, boundary probability per depth (LithoFormer decoupled head), formation-top depth scalar given a prompt (TGS). None parameterise TVT or relative geologic time directly, although WLFM's contrastive positives are defined by relative-depth alignment across wells, i.e. an implicit RGT.
output_representation: Per-depth softmax (zonation), per-depth regression, boundary probability sequence, scalar depth per prompted top; WLFM also outputs discrete geological tokens and embeddings reusable as features.
architecture: WLFM: patch the multi-curve log, encode, vector-quantise (z_q = argmin ||z_e - e_k||) into a learned geological codebook, transformer encoder pretrained with masked-token modelling plus stratigraphy-aware InfoNCE contrastive loss, then multi-task heads with few-shot fine-tuning (RTX A6000, batch 256). LithoFormer: Seq2Seq transformer on the whole log in one pass, channel-independent PatchTST backbone with rotary positional embeddings (RoPE), decoupled multi-task head for zonation and boundary probabilities. TGS: 60M-parameter 1D vision transformer trained as ViT-MAE (masked autoencoding of log patches) on 1.1M logs for imputation, then a promptable head that takes a formation token and regresses its top depth; fine-tuned on 271,972 tops from 44,062 Permian wells, 37 formations. TimeGPT: generic pretrained time-series transformer used zero-shot/fine-tuned for forecasting and anomaly detection. CMT-Hiformer: hybrid CNN-meets-transformer (CMT) blocks inside a hierarchical multi-scale transformer (Hiformer) for per-depth stratigraphic labelling.
core_mechanism: Self-supervised pretraining on many unlabeled wells gives an encoder that maps GR texture to layer identity (WLFM reports emergent layer awareness: same-layer patches cluster across wells, ARI 0.78 and 82.3% purity without lithology labels). The contrastive term explicitly pulls together patches from the same stratigraphic interval in different wells, which is exactly the invariance a lateral-to-typewell matcher needs (same layer, different tool calibration/noise). Geology-informed losses (Law of Superposition, ordering) remove order violations that per-depth classifiers make.
training_objective: WLFM: masked-token prediction over VQ codes + InfoNCE stratigraphy-aware contrastive (positives by relative-depth alignment within tolerance, filtered by low-frequency similarity, in-batch negatives) + downstream task losses. LithoFormer: zonation CE + boundary probability loss + geology-informed penalty enforcing superposition/order. TGS: MAE reconstruction, then depth regression per prompt. CMT-Hiformer: CE plus a geological constraint regulariser with tunable weights that promotes correct boundary placement. TimeGPT: generic forecasting loss (pretrained by vendor).
decoding: Argmax per depth or boundary thresholding (LithoFormer, CMT-Hiformer); direct regression (TGS, TimeGPT); embeddings for clustering (WLFM).
metric_consistent_decode: Mode-seeking (argmax/boundary picks) for the classification models; regression heads approximate the mean. Irrelevant for us if only the encoder is reused as a feature extractor, because our expectation decode stays unchanged.
evidence_scope: Single vertical well per forward pass (whole log in LithoFormer, windows elsewhere); WLFM pretraining uses cross-well pairs, but inference is single-well.
prefix_conditioning: Not applicable (no known-prefix concept). TGS prompting is the closest analogue: the geologist's prompt conditions the output.
propose_vs_select: Single output. As an extra input channel or embedding it would feed our U-Net, not act as a separate ensemble member.
physical_constraints: Superposition / stratigraphic order penalties (LithoFormer, CMT-Hiformer); none on dip, trajectory or TVT+Z identities.
dataset: WLFM: 1,200 wells (Chinese basins [uncertain]), well-level splits, 5 seeds. LithoFormer: three real-world datasets (unnamed in abstract). TGS: 1.1M North American logs pretraining; 44,062 Permian wells / 271,972 tops fine-tuning. TimeGPT-logs: dataset not named in abstract. CMT-Hiformer: Shuanghe oil field, central China.
synthetic_to_real: All real vertical-well data; no synthetic stage. For us the domain gap is large: lateral GR sampled along MD through shallow-dipping strata versus vertical GR in depth; ROGII GR comes with per-well calibration offsets.
metric_and_performance: WLFM: porosity MSE 0.0041 (0.0038 fine-tuned), lithology accuracy 74.13% (78.10% fine-tuned), unsupervised lithofacies clustering ARI 0.78 / purity 82.3%; systematic offsets in shallow and ultra-deep intervals. LithoFormer: about 90% reduction in median boundary error vs baselines, about 80% less manual labour, zero stratigraphic order violations. TimeGPT-logs: R2 up to 0.87, MAPE as low as 1.95%, anomaly-detection accuracy 93%. TGS: formation-top accuracy numbers not in public summary [uncertain]. CMT-Hiformer: improved boundary accuracy vs baselines (numbers not retrieved) [uncertain].
comparability: Not comparable: vertical-well classification accuracy, boundary error or porosity MSE; no pooled TVT RMSE, no laterals, no typewell alignment.
validation_protocol: WLFM uses well-level splits and 5 seeds; others unclear from abstracts. No spatially grouped CV reported; no leaderboard-style blind test.
inference_budget: Encoders of 10-60M parameters over a 1D sequence: milliseconds per well on GPU, seconds on CPU; a precomputed per-level typewell embedding costs nothing at inference. Fits both rig and Kaggle budgets.
repeated_layers: Indirect. A contrastively trained encoder can separate layers that look alike at raw GR amplitude but differ in multi-scale context (WLFM layer-awareness), which could sharpen the matching cost between similar bands. However, truly repeated cycles (same GR signature at different depths) are indistinguishable by any local encoder with a limited receptive field; only longer context or other evidence (neighbour wells, trajectory) separates them. Ordering losses (LithoFormer) prevent order violations in vertical wells; the analogue for us is monotone consistency of band identity along the lateral, which our per-column softmax does not enforce.
drift: Not addressed. Encoders provide texture similarity, not dip estimates.
uncertainty_and_calibration: No calibration analysis reported by any of the five; WLFM reports seed std only. Boundary probability heads (LithoFormer) are uncalibrated probabilities.
where_to_use: (1) As a learned matching-cost channel: pretrain a small 1D GR encoder self-supervised (masked patch + cross-well contrastive) on all typewell GR and lateral GR (real + synthetic), then add channels such as cosine similarity between the lateral-GR window embedding at each MD column and the typewell embedding at each TVT level to the 16-channel cost image, next to gr_abs_diff. (2) Replace tw_gr / gr raw channels with a few PCA components of embeddings (multi-scale context). (3) Borrow the geology-informed-loss idea as a band-consistency regulariser on the U-Net output. The foundation models themselves (weights) are not usable: none are public, and all are vertical-well.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (~51%) via a more discriminative multi-scale similarity cost; possibly broad humps (~13%) via sharper cost. Not drift.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Our cost image uses hand-crafted channels only: tw_gr, gr, gr_abs_diff, windowed GR stats (std, slope, quadratic fit a/b/c, rmse, isnan rate, first-last delta), tw_tvt_rel, seen_tvt_rel, tw_seen_tvt_abs_diff, z_diff (experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_cfg.py unet_static_channels). The only learned similarity is inside the ConvNeXt/FastViT 2D backbone, which is ImageNet-pretrained, not pretrained on log signals. Missing: (a) any log-domain self-supervised pretraining; (b) a learned, calibration-invariant lateral-vs-typewell similarity channel with a long receptive field (hundreds of ft of GR context on both sides); (c) an explicit cross-well invariance objective (WLFM's contrastive positives by relative depth map directly onto our labelled wells: the lateral GR sample at TVT t and the typewell GR at TVT t are a positive pair). Note the 1st place writeup reports transformer backbones lost to ConvNeXt and synthetic-first two-stage training lost to joint training, so the gap is specifically the 1D log encoder as an input feature, not a transformer replacement of the 2D backbone (our axial attention also failed).
proposed_experiment: E1 (cheap, decisive): train a 1D GR encoder (e.g. 4-6 layer 1D ConvNeXt or small transformer, receptive field ~256 ft, 64-d output) with a supervised contrastive/InfoNCE objective on training-fold wells only: anchor = lateral GR window centred at MD column i, positive = typewell GR window centred at the true TVT(i), negatives = typewell windows at other TVT levels, especially the other repeated-band candidates (hard negatives mined from our posterior dumps via seq_NN_posterior_dump.py --save-all humps), plus masked-patch reconstruction on all typewells and synthetic wells as an auxiliary. Add new module experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_gr_encoder.py; compute channel 'gr_emb_cos' (345 x 400 cosine similarity map) in seq_NN_dataset.py next to gr_abs_diff; register it in unet_static_channels in seq_NN_cfg.py (17 channels). First diagnostic without retraining the U-Net: on 155 holdout wells, for multimodal columns, check whether argmax of gr_emb_cos over the sig humps picks the truth hump more often than the dominant hump (76.2% in posterior_geo_pick.py) -- if it does not beat 76.2%, stop. E2: 60-epoch ConvNeXt with the extra channel vs control 5.47 ft, 2 seeds, same folds; then 150 epochs + FastViT KD if positive (>0.39 ft). Fold safety: the encoder must be trained only on training-fold wells for each holdout split, else it leaks labels.
implementation_effort: Medium: ~300 lines (encoder, contrastive data sampler, channel computation, caching of typewell embeddings); fold-safe retraining of the encoder per split adds bookkeeping.
gpu_cost: Encoder pretraining: under 1-2 GPU-hours on RTX 5060 8 GB (1D, small). Channel computation: a 345x400 dot product per well, negligible. U-Net retrain: same as baseline 60/150-epoch runs.
distillation_compatibility: Compatible: the channel is an input, so the FastViT student receives it too; adds one encoder forward pass (few ms) to student inference.
error_correlation_with_ours: Same backbone and decode, so errors stay highly correlated; gains, if any, come from better evidence in the cost volume, not diversity. A standalone embedding-DP tracker using the learned cost could be a more diverse ensemble member.
risk: (1) Our 2D backbone already learns local GR similarity from gr/tw_gr/gr_abs_diff, so a 1D encoder may add nothing (1st place: PF features stopped helping once backbones got stronger). (2) Repeated bands are by definition similar in GR; no encoder with bounded context separates identical cycles, so the gain is capped at the fraction of confusions caused by weak similarity rather than true self-similarity. (3) Only ~773 real wells (54 master typewell systems) supply real positives; synthetic positives may teach synthetic-generator artefacts. (4) Label leakage if the encoder is not fold-safe. (5) No public weights; external foundation models are vertical-well and multi-curve, while ROGII has GR only.
notes: 1st place writeup (1st.txt, 'What didn't work'): transformer backbones and simulation-first pretraining lost. 4th place used a synthetic-only 'foundation model' (5.9 ft CV without real finetuning) as an ensemble member for diversity -- that is the only in-competition foundation-model evidence, and it is a 2D image model, not a log encoder. 5th place synthetic-only model scored 6.34 private. Overlaps A10 (Siamese depth matching) -- the proposed encoder is essentially a Siamese similarity learner; B01 (learned stereo features) is the same idea from stereo. TimeGPT-style forecasting foundation models are not useful here (forecasting GR is not the task). Related CNN+DP alignment: Deep Hierarchical Graph Correlation (JMSE 2026).
